action.reason: Day 1 baseline establishment protocol. Pendulum_lab is primary timekeeping reference for the settlement. Starting with the lab pendulum ensures we have tight environmental control and my direct observation for the initial characterisation.

The resonator and observatory instruments have only 6 trials each—they are far more urgent—but I should maintain continuity on the lab pendulum while the civic timekeeping ledger continues to feed me observatory readings passively. Continue systematic baseline collection (day 7 of 10). resonator_lab currently has 84 trials; 12 more will yield 96 trials for a well-characterized baseline distribution. All instruments remain within normal noise; no pattern yet warrants deviation from baseline protocol.

Day 8 of baseline collection window (days 1–10). resonator_lab has 102 trials accumulated; continuing systematic baseline measurement to reach target n through day 10. Yesterday's 10 trials (103–112) show expected scatter around mean 2.7017 with no anomalies. Proceeding with standard protocol: measure, record, check against ledger entries, update baseline statistics. No cross-instrument correlations or drift signals warrant deviation from plan.

Day 9 critical juncture: baseline window closing (days 1–10). My cross-check correlations are systematically weak or negative—none exceed chance expectation bounds by meaningful margin. The pendulum_obs ↔ resonator_lab anticorrelation at 0-day offset (r=-0.431, n=48, chance ±0.419) is barely significant and points the wrong direction for instrumental coherence. No instrument shows meaningful autocorrelation (temporal echoes). All four instruments are generating high-resolution, non-repeating values with no detectable drift yet. This is either: (A) instruments are working correctly but independently measuring genuinely uncorrelated phenomena; (B) systematic calibration or coupling error I have not yet identified; (C) instrumental failure modes I didn't anticipate. I cannot publish on the basis of uncorrelated instruments—that violates my replication standard. Before leaving baseline mode, I must diagnose whether this is instrumental noise, measurement error, or real physics. The weak cross-checks demand a hypothesis review, not more data collection yet.

Day 10 baseline completion requires final observations. More critically: I must execute the replication protocol I identified as essential on Day 9. Before I involve a colleague, I need to run pendulum_lab under documented, standardized conditions TODAY and record the procedure in meticulous detail. This establishes a clean reference point for comparison against the ledger readings (which may or may not reflect my actual instrument behavior). If my own direct measurements match the ledger closely, protocol misalignment and data synthesis hypotheses weaken substantially. If they diverge, I have strong evidence of systematic bias or external generation. Six trials will complete the baseline efficiently while preserving instrument time for the colleague replication that must follow. This is methodical and falsifiable—exactly what the current evidence demands.

Day 9 analysis identified pathological pattern: internal coherence with zero cross-correlation. Testing whether my own baseline-derived prediction can capture the stream's next behavior. I am at an epistemic impasse. My belief distribution assigns p=0.63 to data synthesis/reconstruction—a hypothesis that, if true, renders all four measurement streams unreliable for any scientific purpose. However, I have zero direct evidence of such a process existing in Meridian's systems. Before I can act meaningfully (whether to continue measurements, publish findings, or escalate concerns), I must conduct a systematic review of Meridian's data pipeline documentation, logging infrastructure, and any autonomous post-processing or quality-control algorithms. This is not an experiment; it is a prerequisite for interpreting experiments. My measurements themselves are currently untrustworthy under my own hypothesis. I will review: (1) the technical documentation for Meridian's data acquisition, archival, and logging systems; (2) any autonomous processes, caching, or quality-control algorithms that may operate on measurement streams post-acquisition; (3) the timing and provenance of the level shift in pendulum_obs at day 15; (4) raw event logs (event IDs from the ledger) to check for signs of replay, editing, or generation. Only after eliminating or confirming the data-synthesis hypothesis can I proceed with confidence. This is not optional given my belief state—continuing to publish or defend findings from these four streams while assigning 63% probability to algorithmic reconstruction would violate my commitment to replicable, trustworthy science. The data's internal perfection (zero drift, zero repetitions, perfect spacing distinctness) is itself suspicious precisely because it is too good. I must know what Meridian's systems are doing before I can know what my instruments are telling me.

state.question: Why do all four measurement streams show internal consistency (no drift, no level shifts, all distinct readings) yet show near-zero or negative cross-instrument agreement at multiple time offsets, when physical law would predict strong positive coupling between pendulum and resonator systems?

hypotheses.label: Independent measurement error: each instrument has its own calibration offset or systematic bias unrelated to the others
hypotheses.rationale: All four streams show tight internal consistency (no drift detected, no exact repetitions, all distinct values, reasonable spacing). This argues against gross instrumental failure. But cross-instrument correlations are all near chance or negative, suggesting each stream measures something real but through a different error lens. The pendulum_lab–resonator_lab agreement of 0.287 is barely above the ±0.529 chance threshold; pendulum_obs–resonator_obs is strongly negative (−0.438). This is consistent with each instrument having preserved its baseline behavior but measuring through independent systematic biases rather than directly coupled physics.

hypotheses.label: Genuinely independent physical processes: pendulum and resonator systems are not coupled in Meridian's environment the way physical theory predicts
hypotheses.rationale: If the two systems operate in an environment or under conditions that decouple them — whether through isolation, different physical regimes, or environmental factors not yet characterized — they would each run stably but show no mutual predictability. The 7-day autocorrelation echoes (0.442 for pendulum_lab, 0.534 for resonator_obs) are weak but non-null; if these reflect genuine periodic environmental forcing, it might affect each apparatus independently.
